name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.214.0 — walkthrough contract: the pushRound example's journey beats now hash its own two steps (f5eac39a8e33, was the four-step story's 08363cd98ef8) in request, response and the pullApprovals echo; a not-found 404 code names an unknown address under /v1 and raises revision to 2 (additive per compatibility); a contract-files test replays every example journey's beats against beatHash of its steps. 7.213.0 — Subtraction pass over the rule prose: text a script already enforces shrinks to a pointer (queue verbs and exits, the status blocks, replay's record matrix, release exit codes, the mocks marks and ledger grammar, init ordering, the marker hook), rules stated in several files collapse to their core.md home (dismissed-question STOP, worker git and MCP bans, decomposition, the retired replay block, Gotchas format, look-stop contract, import layers, never-push, enforce's deterministic-first), and seven derivable confirms print 📌 Auto-picked lines instead: escape's spec pick, field classification and duplicate check, build's out-of-plan gate failure, doctor checks 18 and 21 inside --fix, plan's unbuilt-dependency warning and its too-small-for-a-spec stop. 7.212.0 — Core doctrine § token discipline drops the clause that a pre-existing bug found on the way is reported, not fixed; it contradicted the Incident Policy's fixed-in-the-same-session rule and steered sessions to defer small fixes.
